newsitem.title: USA: U.S. businesses say they face barriers in Japan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. businesses say they face barriers in Japan.

text.p: U.S. business leaders believe that they face unfair barriers in Japan's market and that Tokyo is not doing enough to address those concerns, a survey released on Monday said.

The survey of business executives conducted for the Economic Strategy Institute think tank said that about 78 percent of the executives surveyed believe U.S. firms frequently face unfair barriers that prevent them from competing in Japan.

At the same time, 87 percent believe U.S. markets are largely open to Japanese goods and services with few unfair barriers. While 57 percent of those surveyed believed the U.S. government was doing enough to open Japanese markets, some 78 percent said Tokyo was not open and forthcoming in trying to resolve U.S. concerns about Japanese trade practices.

The telephone survey of 204 senior executives of companies actively involved in Asian trade showed that business leaders are unsure whether the World Trade Organization (WTO) will be effective in resolving U.S. complaints about Japanese trade practices.
The survey was conducted by Geoffrey Garin of Hart Research Associates.

Some 67 percent said it was too early to tell how effective the WTO will be. About half of the executives surveyed said they were familiar with Eastman Kodak Co.'s complaint about barriers in the Japanese film and photographic paper markets, according to the survey.

An overwhelming majority, 85 percent, thought the case had important implications for many U.S. companies. More than half, 53 percent, said that if the case is lost it would reflect more on the inability of the WTO to deal with such trade complaints than a weak case presented by Kodak and the U.S. government.
